haiku-low.q1: They get the same generic reply as a known address. No reset row, no token and no email are created.
haiku-low.q2: The count is 3 or more, so the request commits and gets the same generic reply. No reset row and no email job are created.
haiku-low.q3: A link lives 30 minutes. A newer link issued for the account invalidates it, and using it ends it.
haiku-low.q4: The link stays usable and unused until it expires. The browser gets a form error.
haiku-low.q5: None. Every session for the account is deleted. The user is sent to /login and is not logged in automatically.
haiku-low.q6: The worker retries 3 times with backoff, then clears the payload, logs it and drops the job. The user is not told.
haiku-low.q7: The raw token is encrypted with the app key inside the queued email job. The worker decrypts it and puts it in the emailed link.
haiku-low.q8: It hashes the raw token with SHA-256 and finds the reset row by token_hash. It is live if not used, not invalidated and not expired.
haiku-low.q9: In the password_reset_tokens table, counting rows created in the last hour. Requests drop out by time. Rows are purged after 24 hours.
haiku-low.q10: In the same transaction as the new link, before the new row is inserted, older unused links are invalidated at once.
haiku-low.q11: Password update, deleting all sessions, marking the reset row used and queuing the email all commit together. The confirmation email job is inserted within that same transaction.
haiku-low.q12: The transaction locks the reset row and rechecks it is live. The second submit waits on the lock, then sees it used and gets the expired page.

sonnet.q1: They see the same generic 200 reply as for known addresses. Nothing is sent: no row, no token, no email.
sonnet.q2: Once 3 or more reset rows exist for the account in the last hour, no reset row or email job is created. The user gets the same generic 200 reply.
sonnet.q3: A link expires 30 minutes after it is issued. It can end sooner if it is used, or invalidated because a newer link was issued.
sonnet.q4: The link is not used up. It stays usable until it expires, and the user gets a form error.
sonnet.q5: None. All the account's sessions are deleted. The user is redirected (303) to /login and must log in again with the new password, because there is no automatic login.
sonnet.q6: The worker retries up to 3 times with backoff, then clears the payload, logs it and drops the job. The user is not told. They still saw the generic reply, and the link stays live but unseen until it expires after 30 minutes.
sonnet.q7: The raw token is encrypted with the app key and stored in the email job. The worker decrypts it with the app key and sends it in the email. The payload is cleared after the job is sent or dropped.
sonnet.q8: The server hashes the raw token from the URL with SHA-256 and finds the reset row by that hash. The link is good if the row is live: not used, not invalidated and not expired.
sonnet.q9: It is not kept as a counter. It is counted from the password_reset_tokens rows (used and invalidated ones included) created in the last hour, using an index on (user_id, created_at). Requests drop out as their created_at passes one hour. Rows are purged after 24 hours.
sonnet.q10: The older unused reset rows are invalidated in the same transaction in which the new row and email job are written (step 4 of Flow 1, before the commit). Their pages then show the expired page, and the worker's live check drops their queued emails.
sonnet.q11: In one transaction: update users.password_hash, delete all of the user's sessions, mark the reset row used, and insert the "password changed" email job, then commit. The job is inserted inside that transaction, before the commit. If any write fails, everything rolls back.
sonnet.q12: The confirm step locks the reset row inside a transaction and re-checks that it is live. The second submit waits on the lock, then sees the link used and gets the expired page.
